name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.116.0 — Citation checker verifies the whole heading name, not just the namespace prefix before the first colon. A colon no longer terminates the captured citation name, so a citation naming a section like 'Genesis: Design State' against a file whose headings are 'Genesis: Brief State' and 'Genesis: State Machine' now reports MISS instead of counting as CHECKED on the shared 'Genesis' prefix. The untruncated-window prefix check was extended to the full heading so ordinary prose continuing past a real heading name still resolves. One stale citation the widening exposed (design.md's pointer at a genesis design state that the design-stage re-chain removed) is repointed at Genesis: Brief State; MISS stays 0 repo-wide. 7.115.0 — citations-check.js resolves a path-form lookback token against the repo root instead of skipping it as not-found, and unions genesis.md into the targets for a Genesis-namespaced heading whose lookback names another file — eight previously unchecked doctrine citations now verify, and the live corpus stays at MISS=0. 7.114.0 — the design atlas gains a screen index and two-way note navigation: `page()` carries the `#shell`/`#toc`/`.tocgroup`/`.tochead`/`.tocrow`/`.tocempty`/`#tocbtn`/`#tocscrim` register and `buildAtlas` alone emits the markup (a gallery still renders none), so `design/atlas/index.html` has a sticky index column at wide widths and an off-canvas overlay below 1200px — one row per journey, screen and candidate, a search box filtering the index only, the existing status chips filtering index and cards together, a heading jumping to its section and a row to its card, and a current-section marker derived from a scroll threshold (an IntersectionObserver band was executed and marked nothing). `/__notes/list` gains `screen=**` (every note, no scope filter; `screen=*` and `screen=<label>` byte-for-byte unchanged), so the atlas project panel reaches a note written about one screen: it renders a `button.nl-anchor` labelled `<screen> · <state>` that opens that screen in the lightbox when the card carries an `iframe.frame`, an inert `span.nl-anchor.plain` when it does not, and the screen alone when the note carries no state; a served mock page's strip keeps its `<b>` id badge and gains one `a.nl-up` back to the panel. No deep link into a state. Also: the gate caps test-file parallelism at `--test-concurrency=3`, and three prose-size caps rise ten lines each.
